themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK, a 300% increase from the 1.0 weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a potential coordinated environmental vandalism problem or sudden enforcement gap in Central Harlem's urban forest.
evidence: 4 illegal tree damage complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.24)
300% spike in a category historically low-volume suggests either new problem or sudden concentration
Community Board has flagged 'New equipment for maintenance' for Parks & Recreation in repeated budget requests, indicating pre-existing maintenance infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to document visible tree damage and identify pattern (geographic, type of damage, timing)
Interview Parks Department about response capacity and whether this reflects enforcement blind spots or new illegal activity (development prep, land clearing)

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 5 LAST WEEK, a 400% increase from the 1.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a localized enforcement gap or new supply pattern in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.62)
400% increase in a public safety category warrants immediate mapping and pattern analysis
Community Board repeatedly requests homeless services upgrades, suggesting underlying socioeconomic drivers may be present
reporting_angles: Map the 5 complaints to identify geographic hotspot; check if clustered around parks, transit, or residential blocks
Interview NYPD about enforcement strategy and whether this reflects known open-air markets or new activity

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints surged to 11 LAST WEEK, a 319% increase from the 2.6 weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks, indicating either a sudden sanitation service failure or acute waste management problem affecting households.
evidence: 11 residential disposal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.66)
319% spike coinciding with broader sanitation indicators: 'Unsanitary Condition' is the 5th-highest complaint category overall (1,212 in 90 days)
Related spike in Litter Basket Request complaints (3 last week vs. 0.2 avg, +1100%) suggests overflow or collection failure
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to determine if there was a service disruption, missed pickups, or staffing shortage last week
Visit affected blocks to document waste accumulation; interview residents about collection frequency and conditions

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Emergency Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 700% increase from the 0.4 weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a water infrastructure failure or acute housing maintenance crisis affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: 3 plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42)
700% spike in a category where Central Harlem averages 827 complaints over 90 days (9.2 weekly), suggesting acute concentration
Broader context: HEAT/HOT WATER is highest complaint category overall (4,251 in 90 days), indicating systemic housing infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Map the 3 plumbing complaints; check if they're in same building or contiguous blocks (water main break vs. individual unit failures)
Contact DEP to check for main breaks; interview affected residents and landlords about repair timelines

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Noise in parks complaints jumped to 7 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 600% increase from the 1.0 weekly baseline over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a public disorder or event management problem in Central Harlem's park system.
evidence: 7 park noise complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.54)
600% spike suggests acute event or enforcement gap rather than seasonal summer uptick (data is from mid-range of year)
Related: Community Board has requested 'New equipment for maintenance' for Parks for multiple years, indicating pre-existing resource constraints
reporting_angles: Identify which parks received complaints; check Parks Department event permits and response logs for that week
Interview Parks enforcement about staffing and whether specific parks are chronic hotspots
